lens: Recruitment operator — long or difficult content; simulated expertise/user lens
reason: The inspected local implementation supports deliberate closure and intelligible recovery: current coverage separates submitted observations from valid independent work, closing warns that reopening is unavailable, and batch release reviews exact outcomes with per-applicant blockers and dossier links. I traced the operator journey from round coverage through confirmation, results and release recovery in source and supplied tests. The synthetic mobile close capture is legible, although its explanation and actions require substantial scrolling. The public proposition is coherent with Precision Instrument, describes student consulting and uses an honest pending-approval boundary for case studies. Applicant materials accurately disclose original-resume access. These are promising local mechanisms, not observed operator success. Large-cohort review remains cumbersome in source, and there is no authenticated integration or operator-task evidence sufficient to establish world-class acceptance or release readiness.

findings.evidence: ReleaseAllButton.itemList maps every reviewed decision into one undivided list; confirmation renders itemList(review) before the release and cancel buttons. There is no search, blocker filter or outcome grouping. The 500-decision test at src/app/api/admin/decisions/route.test.ts:287-306 validates request forwarding with mocked RPC results, not reviewing that many rendered rows.
findings.userImpact: An operator reviewing a long cohort must scan eligible and blocked outcomes together and traverse the entire list to reach confirmation. Finding a particular blocked applicant or checking the distribution of difficult outcomes is unnecessarily laborious. This is a source-based usability concern, not a measured task failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Add applicant-code search and explicit blocked/outcome filters with persistent cohort totals and a clearly reachable action area. Keep the complete reviewed snapshot authoritative when filtering, and verify a mixed large cohort in the operator UI.

notVerified: No staging, hosted acceptance, real operator session or human usability study exists; source tracing and intercepted browser tests do not establish observed task success.
Clerk session expiry, actual hosted RPC/RLS authorization, storage access and notification delivery across the complete operator journey were not exercised.
Long names, lengthy evidence notes, many rubric criteria and hundreds of mixed release outcomes have no inspected authenticated visual/task evidence. The supplied close modal is synthetic.
Coverage is explicitly advisory until freeze; this review does not prove every concurrent grading/closure race or recovery after an intentionally irreversible closure.
Physical devices, assistive technology, Safari and Firefox remain unverified. Board resolution of original-resume policy and client publication approval remain external dependencies.
